raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Batch routed-expert (R3) arrays at existing IPC boundaries without delaying incremental delivery. This addresses return-path overhead related to #56402 and investigated in [fork PR #105](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/105); it supersedes the finish-only experiment, which lost partial R3 on frontend abort.

## Claims

- Approximately 19% higher output-token throughput in the original repeated Nemotron/GB200 comparison below; not a universal speedup claim.
- Preserve incremental output, including partial R3 on frontend abort and pause(abort).
- No scheduler, model-runner, async-output, or GPU-to-CPU scheduling changes. With R3 disabled, array packing is skipped; the appended optional wire field adds one nil byte, so wire bytes are not identical.

## Validation

Workload: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, 128 DAPO prompts × 8 samples, 1,024 requests and 7,487,984 output tokens per run. TP1/DP4/EP on one four-GPU GB200 node; Multiproc, async scheduling, prefix caching, R3 and sampled-token logprobs enabled; batch 128, token budget 16,384, GPU memory utilization 0.45.

Original native-versus-batching comparison (October 7 image):

| Version | Runs | Median makespan (range), seconds |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native R3 return path | 3 | 259.412 (259.274–276.016) |
| Incremental batched return path | 2 | 217.910 (213.488–222.332) |

All runs returned valid R3 shapes and logprobs for all requests, with zero output-length mismatches. The finish-only PR105 also ran (196.050, 203.901 seconds), but is not adopted because it regresses partial-output behavior. Profiling and checksum instrumentation are excluded from throughput timings.

Original image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:5fb6d1fb15ff53a3e0fce4bd59661cdc73067b8a09ae40f6d60226c394e33857`, source `bb87d227d4b964abb2a966cdf9194f3d376d9bbe`.

Latest-image validation (October 11): rebased on exact image source `2eb491e18b1ce5b8a25e4c88f32dbb5d028d525c`, preserving its weight-version wire field, Rust boxed payload, and stop-string trimming. The retained batching implementation ran in 223.217 and 212.708 seconds with the same request/token/shape/logprob checks. A proposed singleton no-copy shortcut ran in 217.943 and 227.316 seconds; aggregate throughput was 2.10% lower with inconsistent paired signs. No stable improvement was established, so that extra branch was removed. These October 11 runs compare batching against that rejected shortcut, **not against native vLLM**, and do not establish a new native-baseline speedup.

Latest image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:514cd42702d29a7b8efe20b0a916523ac473ecebdec8d53b1a0d0f5439a48634`. Model revision `bee7596271d1495f6992ae224aefde4410e816b8`; dataset revision `65877096c24ffa7abc4e4fa5edb95cf3413a5674`.

Recipe limitation: PR105's original CuteDSL MoE selection is rejected for this W4A16 checkpoint. All comparisons consistently use Marlin instead; this is not a verbatim reproduction of the unsupported original command.

Correctness and local tests:

- Earlier diagnostic execution verified worker → EngineCore → frontend → final-array checksums for 1,088 outputs including warmups, with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Cross-run bit equality is not claimed: BI=0 can change routes across executions.
- Final latest-image diagnostic (Slurm 35651) passed all 80 final checksum checks, including 64 warmups and 16 deliberately terminated requests: eight frontend aborts and eight pause(aborts). Each preserved correct R3 rows and logprobs in an owning, writable array. A 1,553-token prompt executed chunks of 512, 512, 512 and 17 tokens. Checksums verified worker → EngineCore → frontend → final array within the same execution, with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The diagnostic's 16 length mismatches are expected early termination against a 512-token budget, not failed output checks.
- 99 Python tests passed; 33 pre-existing gated-tokenizer cases deselected because their checkpoint is unavailable. Coverage includes real reusable-SHM-slot ownership, native Ray roundtrip, missing versus empty rows, abort, resumed accumulation, uint8/uint16, weight-version preservation, and stop trimming limited to the current chunk.
- 134 Rust tests passed serially, including real Python inline/OOB fixtures. Latest-rebase Clippy (`--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`) and changed-file pre-commit passed.
- Existing Aux CPU tests are now collected by the existing V1 Others CPU CI job. Engine/executor and Rust tests already have CI collectors.
- Scope: the Nemotron recipe does not enable speculative decoding. The synthetic 1,553-token prompt exercises four prefill chunks but is below the aligned 4,176-token block, so it does not establish a GPU prefix-cache hit. No GPU spec/prefix-hit or Mooncake-runtime compatibility claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local commands</summary>

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/v1/executor/test_ray_utils.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q \
  -k 'not incremental_detokenization and not request_stream_interval_raises and not logprobs_processor and not stop_token and not stop_string and not iteration_stats and not lora_request_tracking and not test_abort_requests'

cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-engine-core-client \
  --lib --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1
```

[Reproduction scripts and results](https://gist.github.com/aoshen02/377db5658721d30b934e9a227a3c19fa). The separate `latest-image-results.json` records October 11's pinned image, all four throughput runs, rejected-shortcut decision and final retained-variant diagnostic. Raw logs and site-specific Slurm/image-overlay scripts remain local. Diagnostics and benchmark scripts are not part of the production diff.
</details>

### October 16 review refinements

Packing, unpacking, accumulation and stop trimming now live under Aux; common engine code retains only fields and guarded calls. CPU wire tests use fixed inline/OOB protocol samples rather than executing Rust-tree files. Length, dtype and trailing-shape checks raise explicit errors under optimized Python as well.

Validation on the latest-main merge: 111 Aux/output-processor tests passed, with 34 gated-tokenizer-dependent cases deselected; the initial broader run hit a Hugging Face 403 in the existing watermark test. Seven protocol checks also passed under `python -O`. Twelve selected SHM-ring/serialization checks passed. Changed-file pre-commit passed. The full Rust suite and GPU model throughput were not rerun for these refinements; the earlier GPU/Rust results above describe the earlier implementation.

CPU-only synthetic transport measurements from the review session (30 samples per arm, six warmups, alternating arms; actual SHM queue, msgpack and frontend accumulation):

| Requests × rows per step × steps | Native per-request | Refined packing |
|---|---:|---:|
| 128 × 1 × 32 | 30.48 ms | 13.22 ms |
| 4 × 4096 × 4 | 8.18 ms | 14.97 ms |

These are synthetic pipeline timings, not GPU throughput or an exact historical-checkout A/B. Large contiguous payloads still pay packing-copy overhead; long-prefill end-to-end A/B remains outstanding. The earlier decode-heavy Nemotron gain does not establish a long-prefill speedup.

Re-run commands:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q \
  -k 'not incremental_detokenization and not request_stream_interval_raises and not logprobs_processor and not stop_token and not stop_string and not iteration_stats and not lora_request_tracking and not test_abort_requests and not watermark_status_partitions_finished_requests'

PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -O -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py -q \
  -k 'unpack_rejects_invalid_row_counts or packing_rejects_mixed_profiles'

PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py -q \
  -k 'broadcast_retains_values_after_ring_reuse or numpy_array_serialization or payload_buffer_reuse or zero_copy_frames_survive'
```

### Unified worker payload

Worker-to-EngineCore output now uses only `rows + spans`; the separate `materialized` dictionary and lookup fallback are removed. Historical R3 is still read after whole-batch publication, then appended to the same packed array as current-step rows. This preserves request token ranges and partial-output behavior, but copies historical results into the step array once more. The earlier GPU throughput results predate this simplification; its end-to-end throughput impact has not been measured.

The mixed same-batch producer/prefix-consumer test checks both outputs share the packed array. The reusable-SHM-slot test now covers both request spans in that single array. The related Aux/output-processor suite passed 111 tests (34 gated-tokenizer cases deselected); changed-file pre-commit passed.

### Capture/unpack cleanup

Removed redundant ndarray conversion in capture, used one slice assignment for both single-row and multi-row writes, and passed the already-checked packed payload explicitly to unpacking instead of checking for `None` twice. Length, dtype, shape, contiguity and buffer-ownership checks remain intact. The frozen final sources passed 111 Aux/output-processor tests (34 gated-tokenizer cases deselected), seven protocol checks under `python -O`, and changed-file pre-commit including mypy. A CPU-only capture-loop diagnostic measured 5.12 ms before versus 4.42 ms after (128 requests × 32 one-row captures; 30 alternating measured samples per arm); this is not GPU throughput. GB200 A/B runs for both the unified worker payload and this cleanup are still in progress; no new end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Details

The overhead comes from transporting many tiny NumPy arrays and retaining one array object per incremental chunk. Reduce representation overhead at transport boundaries while preserving existing delivery and lifecycle semantics:

```text
Worker accepted rows
  -> one step array + request spans (including materialized history)
  -> existing EngineCore output thread packs one array + row counts
  -> frontend reconstructs per-request fields
  -> request-owned bytearray
  -> writable final output at existing finish/abort points
```

Mainline #61000 already copies out-of-band SHM payloads before releasing reusable queue slots; this PR does not add another Aux-specific deserialization copy. Ordinary completed requests transfer their request-owned bytearray to the final NumPy view and drop the accumulator reference; resumable streaming-input requests still copy so later appends cannot alter an earlier result. Rust reuses existing ndarray/frame decoding and restores its per-request payload. Clients must upgrade with the R3-enabled wire change. Packing adds CPU copies and bytearray has allocation slack; this is not a zero-copy or lower-RSS claim.

No open duplicate was identified in October 11 checks: #57966 omits prefixes, #57968 adds Mooncake keys, #59567 batches sampling masks, and #52723/#56778 add terminal Rust/gRPC payload support rather than this incremental IPC batching. Mooncake's keys-only frontend does not carry the full arrays targeted here; worker-tail batching would need separate measurements and preservation of `block_keys`. No speculative Mooncake performance PR is included.

AI assistance was used for implementation, audits, tests, benchmarks, and this description. Claude Code and Kimi K3 completed earlier adversarial rounds. At the submitter's request, Kimi K3 performed the final independent review and a follow-up challenge round, with no identified supported-path blocker; Claude did not review the latest rebase because of its weekly quota. The human submitter confirmed line-by-line review and relevant tests on October 11. Final Rust formatting was checked with the pinned 1.95 toolchain.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Existing IPC boundaries; scheduler and GPU execution unchanged.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Latest-image final diagnostic and CPU/Rust checks passed; coverage limits stated. Final independent Kimi K3 review completed.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Existing test suites and serialization helpers reused; CI test collection added.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Human review/tests confirmed, measured evidence published, and final independent audit completed.
</details>
